description: Original 1909-era Blériot XI monoplane donated to the museum on 28 November 1961; displayed in the restored former engine hall with the Fw 44 and the Anasagasti car since March 2025.

Latécoère 25-3R mail plane operated by Aéropostale/Aeroposta Argentina 1929-1936 and flown by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry; the only surviving Laté 25 in the world. Restored (wings had been stored at the Quilmes technical school) and displayed indoors; confirmed on the museum's 2025 collection page.

Sole I.Ae. 27 Pulqui I, Argentina's first jet (first flight 9 August 1947), restored and displayed indoors in the national-industry hall. Sometimes listed with the fictitious serial C-001; no serial is carried.
aliases: IAe 27; IA-27; Pulqui I; Pulqui; IAe27; IA27

description: Kurt Tank-designed I.Ae. 33 Pulqui II swept-wing jet fighter prototype (the fifth and last airframe built, 1959); restored and displayed indoors. Was loaned to Tecnópolis in 2011-12 and suffered outdoor exposure before returning to Morón.
aliases: IAe 33; IA-33; Pulqui II; Pulqui; IAe33; IA33

description: I.Ae. 22 DL advanced trainer c/n 728, ex Fuerza Aérea Argentina E.a.-701; restored and displayed in Hangar 3 (confirmed November 2025).
aliases: IAe 22DL; IA-22; DL-22; c/n 728; E.a.-701; IAe22DL; IAe22; IA22; DL22

description: IA-35 Huanquero A-316 flew directly to the museum (then at Aeroparque) on retirement in March 1974; displayed indoors. Some English-language lists give the serial as A-305, but the museum and photographs show A-316.
aliases: Huanquero; IA 35; A-305; IA35Ib; IA35; A305

description: IA-53 Mamboretá agricultural/utility prototype PGAX-01, the only example built; displayed indoors.
First IA-58 Pucará prototype AX-01 (first flight 20 August 1969, originally with Garrett engines); restored and displayed indoors.

Fw 44J Stieglitz trainer built under licence in Córdoba (I.Ae. 23 programme, 1937-42) for the Argentine military; serial variously written E.e.-122 / Ea-122. Displayed in the restored former engine hall since March 2025.
IA-50B Guaraní II c/n 06, delivered December 1967 to the II Brigada Aérea as the first photographic-survey Guaraní, retired 8 January 2007; displayed indoors.
aliases: Guarani II; Guaraní; GII; IA 50; c/n 06; IA50B; IA50

description: Second Guaraní II in the collection: c/n 21, delivered to the Army as AE-1001 then to the Servicio Penitenciario Federal as LQ-JXY (1972-1995); in the museum since 1995. Hail-damaged and held in Hangar 4 (restoration/maintenance hangar) per the museum's friends' group; the museum confirmed two IA-50s in the collection in January 2024.
aliases: Guarani II; Guaraní; GII; IA 50; AE-1001; c/n 21; IA50B; IA50

description: Percival Prentice T.1 c/n PAC/F/280, ex-RAF, served the Fuerza Aérea Argentina as E-390; displayed indoors.
aliases: Prentice; P40; c/n PAC/F/280; P40Prentice; P40PrenticeT1

description: Beech B45 Mentor (export T-34A) E-010 of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors (2018 photographs, listed on the museum's 2025 page).
Fleet Model 10A biplane LV-ZCL, formerly kept at the Aeroclub Chivilcoy, transferred by road to Morón on 17 March 2023 and added to the collection; the museum's own page calls it a Fleet 16B.
Fiat G.46-4B trainer c/n 76 of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina (serial E.a.-441); displayed indoors.
MS.760A Paris jet trainer/liaison aircraft E-207 (c/n 015) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors, and one of the museum's Paris had its engine run again in 2025.
Two-seat Mirage IIIDA I-002, one of the first Mirages delivered to Argentina in 1972; arrived at the museum in December 2015 and displayed indoors.
Beech AT-11 Kansan bombardier trainer E-110 (c/n 3495) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed in Hangar 2.

A-4P (A-4B) Skyhawk C-207, c/n 11750, ex-US Navy BuNo 142688; Malvinas veteran that attacked HMS Brilliant (12 May 1982) and HMS Coventry (25 May 1982). Retired March 1999 and at the museum since April 1999; displayed indoors.
aliases: A-4B; A4B; Skyhawk; BuNo 142688; c/n 11750; A4; A4P

description: A-4C Skyhawk C-322, c/n 12839, ex-US Navy BuNo 149514, delivered June 1978, retired March 1999; restored by the GTRA in Malvinas-war markings (completed 2023) and displayed indoors.

IAI Dagger (Nesher) C-432, c/n S-20, flew eight combat missions from Río Grande in 1982 including the 1 May attack on HMS Glamorgan, Alacrity and Arrow; restored at Área Material Río Cuarto and presented in Hangar 3 on 28 July 2022. Sometimes mis-listed as a Kfir C.2.
Canberra B.62 B-109 (c/n HP-176B, ex-RAF WJ609), taken on charge 9 September 1971, retired 5 April 2000 with 1361 flying hours; displayed indoors.
Gates Learjet 25D c/n 25-307, civil LV-OEL; moved into Hangar 3 in March 2025.

MBB Bo 105C c/n S-53, formerly of the Ministerio de Bienestar Social (DINES); restored by the Asociación Amigos del MNA and presented in December 2011. In March 2025 it took the display position of LQ-AOF.
MBB Bo 105CBS of the Policía Federal Argentina (police serial H-6), donated by the PFA; photographed at the museum August 2022 and moved to Hangar 2 in March 2025.
Boeing Vertol Model 308 (CH-47C) Chinook H-91, c/n CG071, ex N37007, of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors (photographed August 2022).
aliases: Chinook; Model 308; N37007; c/n CG071; CH47; CH47C

description: F-86F-30-NA Sabre C-122 (c/n 191-669) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors in current scheme since 2009.
Gloster Meteor F.4 C-041 (delivered as I-041, ex-RAF EE586); displayed indoors.
Ex-Israeli Mirage IIICJ C-712, bought in 1982; arrived at the museum in December 2015 and displayed indoors.
Mirage IIIEA I-011 (c/n 9F/9A), Malvinas-war veteran; arrived at the museum in December 2015 and displayed indoors.
Fokker F28 Mk 1000C T-03 (c/n 11028), former Argentine presidential transport; displayed indoors (2024 visitor report).
Fokker F27 Mk 600 Friendship T-42 (c/n 10346), which flew Malvinas-war supply missions in 1982; displayed indoors with interior open on occasion.
Aero Commander 500U T-137 (c/n 1749-44) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors.
Max Holste MH.1521C Broussard PG-336 (c/n 24C, ex LQ-FZL); displayed indoors.
de Havilland Dove 1 F-12 (c/n 04156) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors (2021 photographs; on the museum's 2025 list).

Douglas C-47A-30-DK c/n 14010, delivered 1962 as air-ambulance LQ-ACF 'Ministro Tiburcio Padilla', to the Fuerza Aérea 1967 (S-3, TS-03, then T-101 from December 1971) and used as a VIP transport; the museum displays it as DC-3 'Independencia' with civil marks LQ-GJT painted. Identity per aerialvisuals and Aeronaves Preservadas; displayed indoors.
aliases: DC-3; DC3; LQ-GJT; LQ-ACF; LV-ACF; c/n 14010; Skytrain; C47; C47A

description: Douglas C-47A-85-DL c/n 19965 (ex NC65283), Fuerza Aérea Argentina T-89 then TA-05; ski-equipped 'El Montañés' was the first aircraft to land at the South Pole from Argentina on 4 November 1965. Displayed indoors.
aliases: DC-3; DC3; NC65283; c/n 19965; Skytrain; C47; C47A

description: DHC-2 Beaver P-05 (c/n 1506) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors.
Grumman HU-16B Albatross BS-02 (c/n G-070) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed indoors.
aliases: Albatross; UH-16B; UH16B; c/n G-070; HU16B; HU16

description: Grunau Baby III sailplane LV-DCR (c/n 7), listed by the museum as 'Baby III'; displayed indoors.
Argentine-built 'Super Albatros AB-I' sailplane/experimental aircraft LV-X-40 listed on the museum's collection page; builder not established.
Morane-Saulnier MS.502 Criquet (French-built Fieseler Storch) c/n 681, civil LV-ZIV; displayed indoors.

Fairchild 82D c/n 66, ex Fuerza Aérea Argentina 151, civil LV-FHZ; the only surviving Fairchild 82 outside Canada. Moved onto the platform during the June 2025 hangar reshuffle; on the museum's 2025 list.
Hiller UH-12E (Hiller 360 family) c/n 2087, civil LV-HEN, ex Dirección de Aeronáutica de la Provincia de Buenos Aires; displayed indoors (2024 feature article).

Bell UH-1H H-15 (c/n 5483) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; third Huey airframe to pass through the museum (an earlier H-19 went to Santa Romana in 2008). Photographed 2017 and on the museum's 2025 list.
Sikorsky S-61R (HH-3F Pelican standard) H-02, c/n 61-763, the only S-61R operated by the Fuerza Aérea Argentina, bought for Antarctic support; displayed indoors.
aliases: Pelican; HH-3F; HH3F; c/n 61-763; S61; S61R

description: Reimar Horten Ho Xb 'Piernífero II' tailless glider built in Argentina; cleaned and structurally restored by the GTRA in 2023 and displayed uncovered indoors to show the wing structure.

Sikorsky H-19A (S-55) H-04, c/n 55-157, ex-USAF 51-3886, Korean-War veteran acquired 1962 by the I Brigada Aérea; in the museum since 1971. Fully restored by the GTRA over three years and formally presented on 9 November 2024.

Cierva C.30A autogiro (Avro 671 Rota) c/n 1031, ex Fuerza Aérea de Chile R-340, civil LV-FBL. Listed by Wikipedia and photographed at Morón in 2014; not on the museum's 2025 web list, so presence should be re-checked on site.
aliases: Cierva C.30A; C30A; Rota; R-340; c/n 1031; R340

description: DINFIA IA-46 Super Ranquel PG-423 (c/n 0216) glider tug of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; restoration by the GTRA completed and the aircraft unveiled in the restored former engine hall on 22 March 2025.
aliases: Ranquel; Super Ranquel; IA 46; c/n 0216; IA46

description: Full-scale wooden development mock-up of the IA-63 Pampa carrying serial EX-03 (not a flying airframe); damaged by outdoor display at Tecnópolis and under repair in Hangar 4 (reported 2023-2026).
Polish-built SBLim-2M (MiG-15UTI) c/n 612304, ex Polish Navy 604, imported to Argentina as LV-X216; never an Argentine military type. On outdoor display on the platform per the museum's 2025 list.
aliases: MiG-15UTI; MiG15UTI; MiG-15; c/n 612304; 604; SBLim2M; SBLim2; MiG15

description: Avro Lincoln B.2 B-004 (c/n 1408, ex-RAF RE351), flown to the museum on 11 March 1968 wearing the serial B-010 of the aircraft originally earmarked. One of only a handful of Lincolns surviving; inside Hangar 4 for GTRA restoration (turrets and Merlin engine work reported 2023 through June 2026), visible on open days.
Bristol 170 Freighter Mk 1A TC-330 (c/n 12751) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; displayed on the outdoor platform per the museum's 2025 list.

C-130B Hercules TC-60 (c/n 282-3656, ex-USAF 61-0969), delivered February 1994 and retired 15 September 2011 with over 22,000 hours; restored by the GTRA and moved inside Hangar 2 in June 2025, with interior tours on open days (2026).
Ex-Austral MD-81 c/n 48025, donated 2013; on the outdoor platform (photographed July 2021, on the museum's 2025 list).
Vickers VC.1 Viking 1B T-9 (c/n 163, ex LV-XET) of the Fuerza Aérea Argentina; on the outdoor platform (2024 feature article).

A-4P (A-4B) Skyhawk C-240, c/n 11917, ex BuNo 142855; Malvinas veteran of the attacks on HMS Argonaut, Ardent and Antelope. Nicknamed 'El Itinerante' for its many moves; disassembled in Hangar 4 awaiting restoration (reported September 2023 and June 2026).
aliases: A-4B; A4B; Skyhawk; BuNo 142855; c/n 11917; A4; A4P

description: Second Chinook (Model 308) H-93, c/n B-802/CG.073, Malvinas-war veteran; in Hangar 4 awaiting restoration as a Malvinas camouflage diorama (reported 2023-2026).
aliases: Chinook; Model 308; c/n CG073; CH47; CH47C

description: Forward fuselage (cockpit section) only of Douglas C-54A-5-DO T-45, c/n 7465; parked in Hangar 4 beside Chinook H-93 awaiting restoration (September 2023).
aliases: Skymaster; DC-4; DC4; c/n 7465; C54; C54A

description: Junkers Ju 52/3m c/n 4043, Fuerza Aérea Argentina T-158 (later civil-marked LQ-ZBD); under long-term restoration in Hangar 4 (GTRA reports May-June 2026).
aliases: Ju 52/3m; Ju52; Tante Ju; LQ-ZBD; c/n 4043

description: BAC One-Eleven 515FB c/n 197, ex-Austral; flew during the 1982 conflict and preserved at Morón since 1993 for fire training. Reported awaiting restoration at the museum (post updated December 2025); a restoration project was shelved for lack of funds.

Swearingen Metro II c/n TC-247, ex Ministerio de Bienestar Social air ambulance, donated December 2012 and moved to Hangar 4 in April 2013; never restored and reported in November 2025 to be parked around the base platform with a proposal to pass it to CIATA.
